subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be categorically denied mutation of legacy ownerless session rows, or should OpenClaw provide a migration or operator-controlled compatibility path?
rationale: Ownerless rows predate the ownership boundary, and fail-closed behavior can intentionally stop existing plugin workflows; repository intent is needed to balance isolation and upgrades.

options.title: Fail closed
options.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows and document the non-plugin or operator recovery path.

options.title: Add migration
options.body: Provide a doctor or explicit ownership migration before enforcing the restriction.

options.title: Preserve temporarily
options.body: Allow ownerless-row mutation during a documented deprecation window with a removal plan.

recommendation.title: Fail closed
recommendation.body: Reject plugin-runtime patches to ownerless rows and document the non-plugin or operator recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: Exact area ownership could not be recovered, so repository leadership is the best available low-confidence route for this policy choice.
